name: enlil-iraq-data-hub
title: Enlil Center Iraq Data Hub: climate, water, energy, economy and governance indicators for Iraq
description: Open mirror of the Enlil Center Iraq Data Hub (https://enlilcenter.org/data): curated time series on Iraq's climate, water, energy, economy and governance, each with its original source, unit, retrieval date and scope notes.

contributors.title: Enlil Center for Environment and Sustainable Development

licenses.name: CC-BY-4.0
licenses.title: Compilation, metadata and documentation; each series also carries its source licence

resources.name: iraq-agriculture-value-added-gdp-share
resources.title: Agriculture, Forestry and Fishing Value Added (% of GDP)
resources.description: Agriculture, forestry and fishing sector value added as a share of Iraq's GDP. Shows the sector is smaller and more volatile than commonly assumed — the 2020 spike reflects the collapse in oil GDP that year, not agricultural growth.
resources.notes: The 2020 spike is a denominator effect from the oil-price collapse, not sector growth.

resources.name: iraq-cip-sectoral-investment-needs-2030
resources.title: Climate Investment Plan: Sectoral Investment Needs to 2030
resources.description: Investment required to 2030 and expected annual economic benefit by sector, as estimated in Iraq's Climate Investment Plan technical report (transitional phase 2025–2030). Total need: US$82.85 billion.

sources.title: Pathways for Climate Investment in Iraq — Technical Investment Report (2025), Table 1
sources.publisher: National Investment Commission / Ministry of Environment, with UNDP

licenses.name: Compiled by Enlil Center from public sources; CC-BY-4.0 for the compilation

resources.notes: Authors' estimation from sector consultations, not audited project pipelines. Enlil Center was a contributing author to the report.

resources.name: iraq-climate-induced-displacement-iom
resources.title: Climate-Induced Internal Displacement (IOM DTM Rounds)
resources.description: Individuals recorded by IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix as displaced within Iraq by drought, water scarcity, salinity and land degradation, across central and southern governorates, by assessment round.

sources.title: Iraq — Climate-Induced Displacement, Central and Southern Iraq (September 2025)

resources.notes: Point-in-time stock figures, not flows. The June 2025 figure was reported as 'more than 168,000' in IOM's Climate Vulnerability Assessment. Rounds are not evenly spaced.

resources.name: iraq-gas-flaring-intensity
resources.title: Gas Flaring Intensity
resources.description: Cubic metres of gas flared per barrel of oil produced — a measure of how much of Iraq's associated gas is wasted relative to output, independent of production volume.

sources.title: Global Gas Flaring Tracker, June 2026 edition — flare volume and intensity estimates by economy, 2012–2025
sources.publisher: World Bank / Global Gas Flaring Reduction Partnership

resources.notes: June 2026 edition. Intensity has fallen since 2012 even as absolute volumes stayed high, because oil output grew faster than gas capture.

resources.name: iraq-gas-flaring-volume
resources.title: Gas Flaring Volume
resources.description: Estimated volume of associated gas flared at Iraq's oil fields each year, from satellite (VIIRS) observations compiled by the World Bank's Global Gas Flaring Reduction Partnership. Iraq is consistently among the three largest flaring countries in the world.

sources.title: Global Gas Flaring Tracker, June 2026 edition — flare volume and intensity estimates by economy, 2012–2025
sources.publisher: World Bank / Global Gas Flaring Reduction Partnership

resources.notes: June 2026 edition. This edition re-estimates the entire 2012–2024 series at substantially higher volumes than the July 2025 edition, whose data file put 2024 at 18.2 bcm (and 2020 at 17.4 bcm); Enlil articles published before June 2026 cite the earlier edition's figures.

resources.name: iraq-gas-flaring-by-oil-company-2023
resources.title: Gas Utilised and Flared by National Oil Company, 2023 (official)
resources.description: Crude gas produced, utilised and flared by each of Iraq's federal national oil companies in 2023, as the companies declared it to the Iraq Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative. Together they flared 515,663 million standard cubic feet (about 14.6 billion cubic metres), 45.3% of the gas they produced. Missan (73%) and Dhi Qar (78%) flared most of their gas; North Oil flared 8%.
resources.unit: million standard cubic feet (mmscf) per year

sources.title: Iraq EITI Report 2023 (published 31 Dec 2025), Chapter 2, Table 20: crude gas utilization by company

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: Company-declared figures (Arabic report, Table 20). Flared gas is split by IEITI into 'recoverable' (flared for operational reasons, could be used with existing processing units) and gas flared because processing equipment is unavailable (80.5% of all flaring in 2023). Total gas includes associated, cap and free gas. Official volumes are well below the World Bank's satellite estimate for Iraq (24.3 bcm in 2023, see 'Gas Flaring Volume'), which also covers Kurdistan Region fields and international-operator fields not in this table. 1 mmscf = 28,316.8 m³. Data-quality note: Basra Oil Company's 2023 row is almost identical to its 2022 row (e.g. flared 352,135 vs 352,134 mmscf), which suggests carried-over reporting.

resources.name: iraq-ghg-emissions-by-category-2021
resources.title: Greenhouse-Gas Emissions by Source Category, 2021 (1st BTR)
resources.description: Iraq's national greenhouse-gas inventory for 2021 by IPCC source category, from the country's first Biennial Transparency Report. Total 205,328 kt CO₂-equivalent including land use.

sources.title: 1st Biennial Transparency Report of Iraq (2021 inventory), as reproduced in Pathways for Climate Investment in Iraq (2025)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Iraq

licenses.name: Compiled by Enlil Center from public sources; CC-BY-4.0 for the compilation

resources.notes: Key-category analysis table from the 1st BTR (issued June 2025). Categories sum to 205,328 kt CO2e with LULUCF.

resources.name: iraq-co2-emissions-total
resources.title: Iraq CO₂ emissions (total)
resources.description: Total carbon dioxide emissions excluding land use, land-use change and forestry, in million tonnes of CO₂-equivalent.
resources.notes: WDI code EN.GHG.CO2.MT.CE.AR5 (AR5 GWP, excluding LULUCF). World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-co2-emissions-per-capita
resources.title: Iraq CO₂ emissions per capita
resources.description: Carbon dioxide emissions per person, excluding land use change — a measure of the carbon intensity of daily life and the power sector.
resources.notes: WDI code EN.GHG.CO2.PC.CE.AR5. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-cereal-yield-kg-per-hectare
resources.title: Iraq Cereal Yield
resources.description: Average cereal yield across Iraq's wheat, rice, maize and barley production, in kilograms per hectare. A long-run proxy for how water availability and agricultural practice translate into actual farm output, distinct from total production (which also moves with planted area).
resources.notes: World Bank series currently runs through 2023 and does not yet reflect the 2025-26 drought season; the article's 2025-26 wheat figures use International Grains Council estimates cited in press reporting instead.

resources.name: iraq-agricultural-land-share
resources.title: Iraq agricultural land (% of land area)
resources.description: Arable land, permanent crops and permanent pasture as a share of total land area.
resources.notes: WDI code AG.LND.AGRI.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-average-precipitation
resources.title: Iraq average precipitation
resources.description: Long-run average precipitation in depth over the country, in millimetres per year (FAO estimate as reported by WDI).
resources.notes: WDI code AG.LND.PRCP.MM. This is a long-term average, updated infrequently — it does not capture year-to-year drought. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-electricity-generation-by-source
resources.title: Iraq electricity generation by source
resources.description: Electricity generation by fuel and technology — gas, oil, hydropower and solar — in terawatt-hours.

sources.title: Yearly Electricity Data / Statistical Review of World Energy; data processed by Our World in Data

resources.notes: Generation by source, terawatt-hours. Zero-value technologies for Iraq (coal, nuclear, wind, bioenergy, other renewables) omitted for clarity. Source: Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy, processed by Our World in Data.

resources.name: iraq-solar-pv-installed-capacity
resources.title: Iraq installed solar PV capacity
resources.description: Cumulative installed solar photovoltaic capacity connected to Iraq's grid, in megawatts.

sources.title: Renewable Capacity Statistics; data processed by Our World in Data

resources.notes: Converted from gigawatts to megawatts (×1,000). Original source: International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), Renewable Capacity Statistics; processed by Our World in Data.

resources.name: iraq-renewable-electricity-output-share
resources.title: Iraq renewable electricity output (% of total electricity)
resources.description: Electricity generated from renewable sources (mainly hydropower) as a share of total electricity output.
resources.notes: WDI code EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-renewable-energy-consumption-share
resources.title: Iraq renewable energy consumption (% of total final energy)
resources.description: Renewable energy as a share of total final energy consumption — Iraq remains one of the lowest in the region.
resources.notes: WDI code EG.FEC.RNEW.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-renewable-freshwater-per-capita
resources.title: Iraq renewable internal freshwater resources per capita
resources.description: Internal renewable freshwater resources (river flows and groundwater from rainfall within Iraq) divided by population — falling steadily as population grows.
resources.notes: WDI code ER.H2O.INTR.PC. Excludes inflows from upstream countries. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-pm25-mean-annual-exposure
resources.title: PM2.5 Air Pollution, Mean Annual Exposure
resources.description: Population-weighted average annual exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5), the pollutant most associated with open waste burning, dust storms and flaring. The WHO 2021 guideline is 5 micrograms per cubic metre.
resources.notes: Modelled estimates (Global Burden of Disease / WDI). Iraq's exposure has stayed near ten times the WHO guideline for three decades.

resources.name: iraq-gas-flared-share-official
resources.title: Share of Gas Flared by Federal Oil Companies (official)
resources.description: Share of the crude gas produced by Iraq's federal national oil companies that was flared rather than used, as declared to the Iraq Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative. It fell from 53.7% in 2018 to 45.3% in 2023: still close to half of all gas produced. Read it alongside the World Bank satellite series, which measures volume rather than share.

sources.title: Iraq EITI reports 2017, 2018, 2019–2020, 2022 and 2023: crude gas produced, utilised and flared by federal oil companies

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: Company-declared figures covering federal national oil companies only (Basra, North, Missan, Dhi Qar, Midland). Sources by year: 2017, IEITI 2017 report Table 3-22 (558,518 of 1,054,864 mmscf flared); 2018, IEITI 2018 report p.15 (594,452 of 1,107,552 mmscf); 2019 and 2020, IEITI 2019–2020 report pp.17–20, published as daily rates (1,669 of 3,256 and 1,368 of 2,865 mmscf/day); 2022, IEITI 2022 report p.41 (511,346 of 1,099,605 mmscf); 2023, IEITI 2023 report Table 20 (515,663 of 1,139,419 mmscf, about 14.6 bcm). The 2021 report has no gas table; 2016 has company tables in mixed units but no national total; 2015 is excluded because its units are misprinted. Flared = all gas burnt (for operational reasons and for lack of processing capacity). Dhi Qar Oil appears as a separate company from 2018; earlier its fields sit within Basra. The share includes cap and free gas, which is mostly used, so the flared share of associated gas alone is higher. Data-quality note on 2022: the national totals reconcile, but the printed company rows for North, Missan and Dhi Qar do not (utilised + flared does not equal produced); the flared figures appear shifted by one row among those three companies, and read in their arithmetically consistent positions the 2022 company shares (North ~13%, Missan ~74%, Dhi Qar ~78%) match the 2023 pattern. Enlil therefore publishes company-level detail for 2023 only.

resources.name: iraq-solar-pv-yield-by-city
resources.title: Solar PV Yield by City
resources.description: Expected annual output of 1 kW of solar panels at the optimal fixed tilt, kWh per year, from the EU's PVGIS service (SARAH3 satellite data, 14% system losses).

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: PVGIS 5.3 PVcalc API with optimalangles=1 and loss=14. Does not include dust and soiling, which typically reduce output by several per cent in Iraq. The World Bank Global Solar Atlas gives slightly higher long-term values (Baghdad 1,694, Najaf 1,734).

resources.name: iraq-cereal-production-tonnes
resources.title: Cereal Production
resources.description: Total production of cereals (wheat, barley, rice, maize and others) in Iraq. Year-to-year swings track water availability and irrigation restrictions more closely than planted area.
resources.notes: FAO data via WDI; series runs to 2023 and does not yet reflect the 2025–26 drought season, for which Enlil articles cite International Grains Council estimates.

resources.name: iraq-gdp-current-usd
resources.title: Iraq GDP (current US$)
resources.description: Iraq's gross domestic product at current market prices, converted to US dollars. The clearest single measure of the size of the Iraqi economy and its exposure to oil-price cycles.
resources.notes: Converted from US$ to US$ billion by Enlil (÷1,000,000,000). WDI code NY.GDP.MKTP.CD. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-gdp-growth
resources.title: Iraq GDP growth (annual %)
resources.description: Annual percentage growth rate of GDP at constant local-currency prices. Swings track oil output and prices as well as conflict shocks.
resources.notes: WDI code NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-gdp-per-capita
resources.title: Iraq GDP per capita (current US$)
resources.description: GDP divided by midyear population, in current US dollars — a rough proxy for average income.
resources.notes: WDI code NY.GDP.PCAP.CD. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-fdi-net-inflows-gdp-share
resources.title: Iraq foreign direct investment, net inflows (% of GDP)
resources.description: Net inflows of foreign direct investment as a share of GDP. Negative values mean more investment left Iraq than entered it that year.
resources.notes: WDI code BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13. Net FDI has been negative every year from 2013 to 2024 with no exception; the last positive year was 2012.

resources.name: iraq-inflation-cpi
resources.title: Iraq inflation, consumer prices (annual %)
resources.description: Annual change in the cost to the average consumer of a fixed basket of goods and services.
resources.notes: WDI code FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG. Very high values in the 1990s reflect the sanctions-era price collapse of the dinar. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-non-oil-revenue-share-non-oil-gdp
resources.title: Iraq non-oil revenue (% of non-oil GDP)
resources.description: Government revenue excluding oil, measured against the size of the non-oil economy. A read on how much the non-oil economy funds the state that runs it, independent of oil income.

sources.title: IMF non-oil fiscal revenue (redistributed via FRED)
sources.publisher: IMF / Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

resources.notes: FRED series IRQGGRXOGDPXOPT, IMF-sourced, not a World Bank WDI series. 2025 figure is an IMF projection, not an outturn. Re-verified live 24 Sep 2026 (unchanged from a 22 Sep 2026 pull).

resources.name: iraq-oil-rents-share-gdp
resources.title: Iraq oil rents (% of GDP)
resources.description: Oil rents — the difference between the value of crude production and its cost of production — as a share of GDP. A direct read on how oil-dependent the economy is.
resources.notes: WDI code NY.GDP.PETR.RT.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-population
resources.title: Iraq population
resources.description: Total midyear population, counting all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.
resources.notes: Converted from persons to millions by Enlil. WDI code SP.POP.TOTL. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-southern-seaborne-crude-exports-2026-monthly
resources.title: Iraq southern (seaborne) crude oil exports, monthly (2026)
resources.description: Iraq's southern, seaborne crude oil export volumes by month during the 2026 Iran-Israel-US war and Strait of Hormuz crisis. This covers the Basrah export route most directly exposed to the Hormuz closure; Iraq's separate northern Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline route continued operating and is not included here, so it understates Iraq's total national export volume in months when that pipeline was active.

sources.title: Iraq southern crude export volumes, 2026
sources.publisher: SOMO / Iraq Ministry of Oil, as reported by AGBI and Reuters

licenses.name: Compiled by Enlil Center from public sources; CC-BY-4.0 for the compilation

resources.notes: March and April figures were dropped from this series after independent re-verification found conflicting monthly totals across sources that could not be reconciled with confidence; only May-August figures corroborated by ministry-cited (SOMO) reporting are included. This is southern/seaborne (Basrah) volume specifically, not Iraq's total national export volume - the northern Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline route continued operating separately and added several hundred thousand bpd on top of this series in most months (combined national average was roughly 530,000 bpd across May-June, against 100,000-500,000 bpd shown here for the seaborne route alone). Pre-war baseline (Jan-Feb 2026) reflects total exports since the routes were not yet differentiated in reporting.

resources.name: iraq-total-natural-resource-rents-gdp-share
resources.title: Iraq total natural resource rents (% of GDP)
resources.description: The combined rents from oil, natural gas, coal, minerals and forests as a share of GDP — the broadest single measure of how much of Iraq's economy is extracted rent rather than produced value.
resources.notes: WDI code NY.GDP.TOTL.RT.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13. Companion series to iraq-oil-rents-share-gdp — this is the broader total-resource-rent figure (oil, gas, minerals, forest), oil alone accounts for nearly all of it in Iraq's case.

resources.name: iraq-unemployment-rate
resources.title: Iraq unemployment rate (% of labour force)
resources.description: Share of the labour force that is without work but available for and seeking employment (ILO modelled estimate).
resources.notes: WDI code SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS (ILO modelled estimate). World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-urban-population-share
resources.title: Iraq urban population (% of total)
resources.description: Share of people living in urban areas as defined by national statistical offices.
resources.notes: WDI code SP.URB.TOTL.IN.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-official-dinar-rate-tiers
resources.title: Official Dinar Rate Tiers, Central Bank of Iraq
resources.description: The three official dinar-per-dollar rates the Central Bank of Iraq has set since it moved to a tiered structure in December 2020: the rate at which it buys dollars from the Ministry of Finance, the rate at which it sells to banks, and the rate for the public. The latest change, on 7 October 2026, set them at 1,500 / 1,510 / 1,520.

sources.title: Central Bank of Iraq exchange-rate notices: 19 Dec 2020 (news 1624), 7 Feb 2023 (news 2229), 7 Oct 2026 (news 3355)

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: Tiers as worded by the CBI. Third tier: 'sale to the public' in 2020; 'banks and non-bank financial institutions to the final beneficiary' in 2023; 'cash dollars to the public' in 2026. The December 2020 notice is signed 19 Dec 2020 and states no effective date; the February 2023 rates applied from 8 Feb 2023; the October 2026 rates from 7 Oct 2026, under Council of Ministers Resolution 544 of 6 Oct 2026. Before December 2020 the CBI set a single auction price (1,166 from January 2012, 1,182 from December 2015) with small surcharges for transfers and cash, so earlier periods are not shown as tiers; see 'Official Exchange Rate' for the annual series. Notices: cbi.iq/news/print_news/1624, cbi.iq/news/view/2229, cbi.iq/news/view/3355. The parallel market rate is not covered.

fields.name: CBI buys from Ministry of Finance

resources.name: iraq-official-exchange-rate
resources.title: Official Exchange Rate, Dinars per US Dollar
resources.description: Iraq's official dinar-per-dollar rate from 2004 to today. It tracks the Central Bank of Iraq's base rate through the devaluation of December 2020 (to 1,450), the revaluation of February 2023 (to 1,300) and the devaluation of 7 October 2026 (to 1,500).

sources.title: World Development Indicators, official exchange rate PA.NUS.FCRF (2004–2025 annual averages); Central Bank of Iraq notice of 7 Oct 2026 (2026 rate)
sources.publisher: World Bank; Central Bank of Iraq

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: 2004–2025: annual average of the official (CBI base) rate, World Bank WDI series PA.NUS.FCRF. 2026: the official base rate in force from 7 October 2026, set by Council of Ministers Resolution 544 and the Central Bank of Iraq notice of 7 Oct 2026 (cbi.iq/news/view/3355); it is the current rate, not an annual average (the base rate was 1,300 from 1 January to 6 October 2026). The series will be replaced by the World Bank 2026 annual average when published. Tiers in force: 1,500 / 1,510 / 1,520 (see 'Official Dinar Rate Tiers'). The parallel market rate, which has traded above the official rate at times (2022–2023, October 2026), is not covered. Series starts in 2004, after the new dinar replaced the old currencies.

resources.name: iraq-solar-panel-battery-imports-china
resources.title: Solar Panel and Battery Imports from China
resources.description: Value of China's exports to Iraq of photovoltaic modules (HS 854143) and lithium-ion batteries (HS 850760), as reported by China to UN Comtrade. China supplied 99.6% of Iraq's 2025 module imports.

sources.title: China exports to Iraq, HS 854143 (PV modules) and HS 850760 (lithium-ion batteries), 2022–2025

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: Mirror data: China as reporter, Iraq as partner, FOB values. Module code 854143 exists from 2022 (HS2022); earlier years used 854140, which also includes LEDs, so they are excluded. 2025 modules: 3,417,038 items, 101,494 t (about 29.7 kg each); at 550 W per module this is about 1.9 GW (Enlil estimate). Batteries include all uses, not only solar storage.

resources.name: iraq-electricity-transmission-distribution-losses
resources.title: Electric Power Transmission and Distribution Losses (% of Output)
resources.description: Share of electricity generated that is lost in transmission and distribution before reaching consumers. Iraq's losses are among the highest recorded anywhere, a core reason installed capacity translates into far less delivered power.
resources.notes: Includes technical losses and non-technical losses (theft, unmetered use). Values above 50% in recent years reflect Iraq's degraded grid and widespread unbilled consumption.

resources.name: iraq-electricity-load-demanded-supplied-by-governorate-2025
resources.title: Electricity Load Demanded vs Supplied by Governorate, 2025
resources.description: Average load demanded and average load supplied by governorate in 2025, megawatts, from the Ministry of Electricity.

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: Read from the chart on p.35 of the Annual Statistical Report 2025. Nineveh (2,174 MW demanded) is omitted because its supplied value is truncated in the published chart. Federal governorates only; the Kurdistan Region is not included.

resources.name: iraq-access-to-electricity
resources.title: Iraq access to electricity (% of population)
resources.description: Percentage of the population with access to electricity, from household surveys and utility data. Access is near-universal on paper; hours of supply are the real constraint.
resources.notes: WDI code EG.ELC.ACCS.ZS. Measures connection, not reliability or hours of supply. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-energy-use-per-capita
resources.title: Iraq energy use per capita
resources.description: Primary energy use per person before transformation to end-use fuels, in kilograms of oil equivalent.
resources.notes: WDI code EG.USE.PCAP.KG.OE. Series ends where WDI coverage ends. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-total-electricity-generation
resources.title: Iraq total electricity generation
resources.description: Total electricity generated in Iraq from all sources, in terawatt-hours.

sources.title: Yearly Electricity Data / Statistical Review of World Energy; data processed by Our World in Data

resources.notes: Total electricity generation, terawatt-hours, all sources. Source: Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy, processed by Our World in Data.

resources.name: iraq-residential-electricity-tariff-tiers
resources.title: Residential Electricity Tariff Tiers
resources.description: Ministry of Electricity tariff in force for residential consumers, dinars per kWh by monthly consumption band.

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: From the 'tariff in force' table, Annual Statistical Report 2025, p.38. Commercial 60/80/120; industrial and agricultural 60; government 120. The Minister of Electricity put the cost of a kWh at 120 IQD (Nov 2024).

resources.name: iraq-corruption-perceptions-index
resources.title: Iraq Corruption Perceptions Index
resources.description: Transparency International's annual perceived-corruption score for Iraq's public sector, 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean), alongside its global rank.

licenses.name: other-at
licenses.title: See the original publisher's terms of use

resources.notes: Re-verified live 24 Sep 2026: the 2025 CPI (28/100, rank 136 of 182) had been published since the figure was first pulled on 22 Sep 2026 (26/100, rank 140 of 180) — the newer release is used here. Number of countries ranked changed 180->182 between releases, which affects rank comparability more than score comparability.

resources.name: iraq-worldwide-governance-indicators
resources.title: Iraq Worldwide Governance Indicators
resources.description: The World Bank's six governance estimates for Iraq — voice and accountability, political stability, government effectiveness, regulatory quality, rule of law, and control of corruption. Scores run from roughly −2.5 (weak) to +2.5 (strong).
resources.notes: WGI estimates are composite perception-based indices; the World Bank advises treating small year-to-year changes with caution. World Bank data last updated 2026-03-18.

resources.name: iraq-basic-water-and-sanitation-access
resources.title: Iraq access to basic drinking water and sanitation
resources.description: Share of the population using at least basic drinking-water services and at least basic sanitation services (WHO/UNICEF JMP).
resources.notes: WDI codes SH.H2O.BASW.ZS and SH.STA.BASS.ZS (WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme). World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-safely-managed-drinking-water-share
resources.title: Iraq access to safely managed drinking water
resources.description: Share of the population using drinking water free from contamination, available on premises and when needed — a stricter WHO/UNICEF standard than "basic" access. Companion to iraq-basic-water-and-sanitation-access: Iraq reports near-universal basic access, but a much lower share meets this safely-managed standard.

sources.title: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme, via World Development Indicators (WDI)

resources.notes: WDI code SH.H2O.SMDW.ZS (WHO/UNICEF JMP). World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13. Found while researching "The Emergency Iraq Keeps Declaring" (pollution/water-quality piece) — the basic-access series already on the Data Hub (iraq-basic-water-and-sanitation-access, ~98%) understates the quality problem; this stricter standard shows only ~60% as of 2024.

resources.name: iraq-safely-managed-sanitation-share
resources.title: Iraq access to safely managed sanitation
resources.description: Share of the population using sanitation facilities where excreta are safely disposed of in situ or treated off-site — a stricter WHO/UNICEF standard than "basic" access.

sources.title: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme, via World Development Indicators (WDI)

resources.notes: WDI code SH.STA.SMSS.ZS (WHO/UNICEF JMP). World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13. Directly relevant to "The Emergency Iraq Keeps Declaring": only about half of Iraqis have sanitation that is safely managed, consistent with the Ministry of Environment's own June 2026 admission that up to 70% of sewage in some provinces gets incomplete or no treatment.

resources.name: iraq-agricultural-water-withdrawals-share
resources.title: Iraq agricultural share of freshwater withdrawals
resources.description: Share of total freshwater withdrawals used by agriculture (irrigation and livestock).
resources.notes: WDI code ER.H2O.FWAG.ZS. World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.

resources.name: iraq-freshwater-withdrawals-share
resources.title: Iraq freshwater withdrawals (% of internal resources)
resources.description: Annual freshwater withdrawals as a percentage of internal renewable water resources. Values above 100% mean Iraq draws more than its own renewable supply, relying on inflows from Turkey, Syria and Iran.
resources.notes: WDI code ER.H2O.FWTL.ZS (FAO AQUASTAT via WDI). World Bank data last updated 2026-07-13.
